subject: Technology
title: The workshop, the environment and safety

questions.q: What is “technology”?
o: A set of rules we follow to do things by hand.
Technical and scientific knowledge used to create objects that make our lives easier.
A machine that works with electricity.
questions.e: Technology = technical + scientific knowledge used to make useful objects.

questions.q: What is a “technique”?
o: The combination of processes and rules we must follow to achieve something.
questions.e: A technique is the set of processes and rules used to achieve something.

questions.q: In the book, asbestos is an example of a material that…
o: was useful but was later found to be a carcinogen and was banned.
questions.e: Asbestos was used for years, then found to be a carcinogen and banned.

questions.q: How can pollution reach human beings?
o: It travels up the food chain.
It is always easy to see.
questions.e: Pollutants move up the food chain until they reach us at the top.

questions.q: How does acid rain form?
o: When it rains on the mountains.
When polluting gases mix with water in the atmosphere and form acids.
questions.e: Polluting gases + water in the air form acids that fall as acid rain.

questions.q: Which of these is a water pollutant named in the book?
questions.e: POPs — Persistent Organic Pollutants — are a main water pollutant.

questions.q: What does “self-purification” of the soil mean?
o: The soil can absorb some pollution by itself.
The soil makes plants grow faster.
Farmers wash the soil every day.
questions.e: Soil can absorb some pollution by itself — but not when it is excessive.

questions.q: What is the main cause of today’s rapid climate change?
o: The increase in greenhouse gases from human activity.
questions.e: Extra greenhouse gases from human activity drive today’s warming.

questions.q: What do the “3 Rs” stand for?
questions.e: The 3 Rs are Reduce, Reuse and Recycle.

questions.q: What is the correct order of the project method?
o: Define → Search for solutions → Decision-making → Design → Planning and production → Verification.
questions.e: Define → Search → Decide → Design → Plan & produce → Verify.

questions.q: What does “brainstorming” mean?
o: Quickly proposing many ideas, even if they are not all possible.
Copying a solution from a book.
questions.e: Brainstorming = propose many ideas fast, even impossible ones.

questions.q: Morphological analysis studies…
o: the shape, parts, size and colour of an object.
only how the object is used.
questions.e: Morphological analysis looks at shape, parts, size and colour.

questions.q: What is a Gantt chart used for?
o: To control the time given to each task.
questions.e: A Gantt chart controls the time given to each task.

questions.q: Which team member writes down everything the team agrees?
questions.e: The secretary writes down and stores what the team agrees.

questions.q: If there is an accident, what is the PAA approach?
questions.e: PAA = Protect, Alert, Assist.

questions.q: In Spain, what is the emergency phone number?
questions.e: 112 is the emergency number in Spain and across the EU.

questions.q: When does an electrical risk happen?
o: When you touch live wiring or handle a power supply carelessly.
When you use a low-voltage battery.
When you tidy up the workshop.
questions.e: Electrical risk comes from live wiring or careless power handling.

questions.q: A triangular yellow sign with a black pictogram is a…
questions.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 48 48"><path d="M24 5 44 41H4Z" fill="#F2B01E" stroke="#14213D" stroke-width="2.5" stroke-linejoin="round"/><rect x="22" y="18" width="4" height="12" rx="1.4" fill="#14213D"/><circle cx="24" cy="35" r="2.4" fill="#14213D"/></svg>
questions.e: A yellow triangle with a black pictogram is a warning sign.

questions.q: Which colour is used for prohibition or to show danger?
questions.e: Red is used for prohibition and to point out danger.

questions.q: What is air pollution?
o: The presence of harmful or irritating substances in the air.
questions.e: Air pollution = harmful or irritating substances in the air.

questions.q: What is “sustainability”?
o: Using up resources as fast as possible.
Meeting our needs without exhausting natural resources.
questions.e: Sustainability means using resources without depleting them.

questions.q: In the book, “barren” soil is soil that…
o: has no plants growing in it.
questions.e: “Barren” describes soil where no plants can grow.

questions.q: A round sign with a red ring tells you…
questions.e: A round sign with a red ring is a prohibition sign: never do it.

questions.q: What does a round blue sign mean?
o: An obligation — something you must do.
questions.e: Round blue signs are obligation signs: something you must do.

questions.q: Which colour is used for emergency information, like exits and first aid?
questions.e: Green is used for emergency information (exits and first aid).
